title: Select & onboard multilingual cross-encoder rerankers with regression safeguards
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Our current token-prefix reranker (bi-encoder + MLP) serves most rerank workloads, but commercial customers requiring high precision on short candidate sets (search, semantic relevance reordering) are asking for cross-encoder quality. Cross-encoders historically improve nDCG/MRR but are ~5-10x more expensive/latency-intensive. This ticket scopes selecting a small set of cross-encoder variants (including compressed / multilingual variants), validating them across our multilingual evaluation suites, and implementing regression-safe rollout paths that meet latency and cost SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Identify 2-3 cross-encoder candidates (small/medium/quantized) with reproducible offline gains: >= +0.02 nDCG@10 on internal devset and no >0.02 drop on any supported language in multilingual suite

End-to-end p95 latency for rerank endpoint (single-request, 16 candidates) <= 120ms in hosted-prod-staging with optimized kernels and batching, or documented trade-off and capacity recommendations if not achievable
Automated regression tests added to CI: offline eval, smoke on shadow traffic, and metric thresholds that block rollout
Canary rollout plan and automatic rollback hooks instrumented in Console (alerts for quality regressions and cost anomalies)
Documentation: model selection rationale, quantization/distillation settings, and operational runbook published to Confluence
technical_notes: Candidate families: cross-encoder-small-msmarco-v2 (fast), cross-encoder-multilingual-base (XLM-R derived), cross-encoder-distilled-mt (distilled multilingual). We'll also test 8-bit/4-bit quantized variants using runtime quant kernels.

Performance levers to try: autotuned kernel assignment, per-model batch size heuristics (prefer batch-of-1 low latency path), prefix/KV caching for long queries where possible, and candidate sharding across GPUs for >32 candidate lists.
Memory/throughput constraints: 4-bit quantization reduces memory footprint significantly but may change calibration; include per-model calibration step for logits scaling.

Fallback/policy: if cross-encoder latency or cost exceeds thresholds, route to bi-encoder + pointwise reranker as fallback with degraded quality notice and metric tracking. Policy expressed as routing rule in smart-router config: priority=rerank_high_quality -> try cross-encoder -> if p95>threshold or mem spike -> fallback to bi-encoder.
Model packaging: container + model-config including tokenization overrides, max_seq=256, allowed languages list. Include compatibility fields so Dedicated/Private deployments can pin model variants.
evaluation_plan: Offline: run BEIR and MTEB subsets in en, es, fr, de, zh, ja and internal commercial devset. Record nDCG@10, MRR, Recall@5 and latency per-query on standard infra.
Shadow traffic: route 10% of traffic to cross-encoder in shadow mode for 72 hours; compute online relevance deltas (CTR proxy, query-level ranking agreement) and cost per request.
Regression thresholds: block if any language sees >0.02 absolute drop in nDCG@10 or >2% drop in CTR proxy over baseline; also block on increase in 95th latency >25% or cost per query >15%.
Manual review: product/solutions to review examples where cross-encoder differs from baseline for potential semantic regressions (esp. bilingual queries).
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (offline & perf): evaluate candidates locally and with batch infra; pick top 2 by quality/latency tradeoff (ETA +7 days).
Stage 2 (staging canary): deploy model to staging runtime, run 48-hour shadow tests with instrumentation. If metrics meet target, proceed.
Stage 3 (production canary): 2% traffic for 24h -> 10% for 72h -> 50% for 24h. Observe metrics; automated rollback if regression checks fail.
Stage 4 (GA): make model available as rerank variant in API catalog and document cost/perf guidance; include knob for customers to opt-in per route.
Rollback hooks: include automatic revert if regression guardrails or latency SLA violated; manual escalation path to SRE
monitoring_and_regression_checks: Offline nightly job: compute nDCG@10 and MRR across multilingual suite; publish deltas to dashboards and create alert if any delta < -0.01 for 2 consecutive runs.
Production SLOs to track: p50/p95 latency, cost per rerank, traffic-weighted nDCG proxy metric, error rate. Alert thresholds defined in Console dashboard.
Drift detection: tokenization or tokenizer language mismatches can produce systematic drops for certain languages; run per-language breakdown and alert on >1% delta vs baseline.
Canary gating: CI job enforces that any model candidate must pass offline thresholds before creating deployment artifact. PRs that change model artifacts must link to perf report.
Daily regression digest sent to PM/Eng/Research during canary period; include top 50 queries by disagreement.
